provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Out family batch. Highest close value in the family; the kit leans on design-and-build decisions, permits and the backyard as one project. No decking or lumber brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Wood balusters, cable rail, aluminum and glass panels, stair widths and landings, post-cap lights, and what the code asks for at each deck height
pageStructurePlus.why: Railings are the most visible part of a deck from the yard and a big swing in the quote. Owners pick them from pictures, not from a catalogue.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Open pergolas, louvered roofs, solid insulated patio covers, shade cloth and attached versus freestanding, with what each does about sun and rain
pageStructurePlus.why: People ask for a pergola when they want shade, then learn it doesn't stop rain. Laying out the options early prevents a re-quote.

pageStructurePlus.section: Permits, footings and the deck inspection
pageStructurePlus.contains: When a deck needs a permit, footing depth, ledger flashing, railing height, the inspections, and who pulls the permit and meets the inspector
pageStructurePlus.why: A deck attached to the house is a structure. Buyers want to know the builder handles the permit, and that worry decides who they call.

pageStructurePlus.section: Old deck: repair, resurface or rebuild
pageStructurePlus.contains: Soft boards, wobbly railings, rotted joists and ledger boards, new decking over a sound frame, and when the frame has to come out
pageStructurePlus.why: Most deck calls start with a tired old deck. Showing the three paths lets the owner self-sort before you climb underneath.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Deck-to-patio steps, pergola over the dining area, privacy screens, built-in benches, lighting in the stairs, and how the pieces connect to the back door
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers picture a whole outdoor room, not a single deck. A layout page starts the bigger conversation and raises the ticket.

designDirections.name: Back Door Estimate
designDirections.bestFor: Small deck crews that mostly rebuild and resurface, and win on answering fast
designDirections.headlineSample: Decks and patio covers built right in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Citrus warmth reads like a summer evening on a deck, and the geometric caps keep the estimate button loud on a phone.

designDirections.name: Board by Board
designDirections.bestFor: Builders with a deep backlog of finished decks, pergolas and covered patios to show
designDirections.headlineSample: Decks, pergolas and covered patios in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's combo. Slab headings feel like a framing stamp, and the linen ground lets cedar, composite and stained beams carry the page.

designDirections.name: Outdoor Room
designDirections.bestFor: Design-and-build outfits selling multi-level decks with pergolas, lighting and built-ins
designDirections.headlineSample: Outdoor rooms designed and built for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: Driftwood tones sit quietly behind weathered timber, and the refined serif signals a designed project rather than a lumber-yard quote.

openers.line: Your Maps listing for {Business Name} has no website, so someone in {City} deciding between two deck builders can't see a single pergola or railing you've framed before they choose.
openers.hook: Open their Google listing and confirm the Website button is missing. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: This is what that missing button could open: {demo-link}

openers.line: The link on your listing drops people onto your Facebook feed. A couple planning a covered patio wants to see cover styles and ask for a design visit, not scroll past last month's posts.
openers.hook: Tap the listing link and confirm it goes to Facebook. Note the most recent deck or pergola they posted there.
openers.linkLine: A deck and patio cover site instead of a feed: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site still shows the free-host banner and a gallery that stops a few seasons back. Someone about to put a big deck on their house wants to know the builder is still building.
openers.hook: Look for a builder banner, an old copyright year or a newest project that is clearly a few years old. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Same deck builder, up to date: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your deck gallery loads as one long column of thumbnails with no way to open them. Most people browse decks on the couch, phone in one hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Open it on a phone and note what fails: gallery, menu or the call link. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your deck gallery, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to ask {Business Name} for a deck design visit except by calling. People sketch their deck on a napkin at night and would gladly send the size, the height off the ground and a yard picture.
openers.hook: Check their listing, social bios and any site for a form. If calling is the only path, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A design-visit form that asks deck size, height and boards: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Pergola work buried in the feed
openers.line: The cedar pergola and the two-level composite deck on your Instagram are the kind of work people save. Right now they sit between truck posts and lumber deliveries.
openers.hook: Find two finished projects on their grid you can name by type and material. Use one by name if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your decks and pergolas, sorted by project type: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews mention a deck that passed inspection first time and a crew that protected the flower beds. Nobody reads those unless they're already on your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one line about a deck, patio cover or inspection. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews beside the decks they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Deck builders who get their design visits booked in January start framing in April. The ones homeowners find in the cold months are the ones with a full outdoor season.
openers.hook: Use from December to early March. Mention the month and how far their backlog usually runs if they post about it.
openers.linkLine: Ready for the winter deck planners: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most people plan a deck after the kids are in bed, which is when your phone is off. A request form that asks the right questions catches them at ten at night.
openers.hook: Call the listed number after hours. A full or generic voicemail means the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A deck request that works after dinner: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a deck carpenter. Good framers look at a builder's work online before they apply, the same way a homeowner does.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note, a story or a sign. Note the date and the role.
openers.linkLine: A deck builder site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You build decks and patio covers well beyond {City}, but nothing online tells a homeowner in {Neighborhood} you'll come out there. That town name is what they search with.
openers.hook: Find the towns named in their project captions or reviews. Use the one furthest from their shop.
openers.linkLine: A deck page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you finance decks and pergolas, say it before the design visit. A full backyard deck with a cover is a number most families want split into payments before they call.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing anywhere: a post, a review, the truck. Otherwise skip this angle.

openers.line: A deck bolted to the house needs a permit and an inspector's sign-off. A page that shows your licence, insurance and how you handle the permit answers the question a careful buyer asks first.
openers.hook: Check the state contractor registry and confirm a record exists. Never quote a licence number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and permits on one deck page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like a lot of your deck work comes from neighbours leaning over the fence at a finished job. Even those neighbours look you up before they call.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'saw the deck next door' or 'neighbour recommended'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next neighbour's deck referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you finished is a deck people stop and look at. It deserves to be the first project a stranger sees, not a post that slides down the feed by Friday.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished deck, patio cover or pergola and name it exactly: material, levels, railing, town if tagged.

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is a good-looking deck.

I looked for deck builders in {City} and found {Business Name} on Instagram and Maps, but no site where someone can see your pergolas and ask for a design visit. I mocked up a sample deck site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my note got buried. Here's the sample deck and patio site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has projects sorted by deck, pergola and covered patio, a design-visit form that asks size and height off the ground, and a permits page. If it's not for you, say so and I'll drop it.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}. I build websites for deck builders here in {City}. I sent you a message about a sample site, did it reach you?"

IF NO:
"No problem. Short version: I put together a sample deck site for {Business Name}, with your decks, pergolas and patio covers sorted by type and a design-visit form, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link to look at tonight?"

IF YES:
"What did you make of it?"
 → let them talk
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many project and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a deck outfit your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is a small slice of one deck."
"Can we look at it together for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday evening?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before the spring design rush."

objections.handler: "Good problem. The site lets you pick the bigger deck and pergola jobs instead of taking whoever calls first, and the form filters out the small repair calls you don't want."

objections.objection: My work comes from referrals and neighbours.
objections.handler: "That says the decks sell themselves. The neighbour still searches your name before calling, and right now they land on a feed. The site is where that referral lands."

objections.objection: My nephew is building me a site.
objections.handler: "Then you're covered. Happy to hand over the project gallery layout and the design-visit form if they help. If it stalls before spring, the offer stands."

objections.objection: I don't have time to write anything or gather pictures.
objections.handler: "You don't write it. I build it with marked placeholders, you send me project pictures from your phone when you're on a lunch break, and I write the captions from a ten-minute call."

objections.objection: I already pay for leads from a lead platform.
objections.handler: "Those deck leads go to several builders at once and you pay either way. Your own site sends the person who saw your pergola straight to you."

objections.objection: Everyone just wants the cheapest deck.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the buyers who care about footings, ledger flashing and a railing that doesn't wobble. That's what makes your number make sense."
"{Build Range}. For you it'd be about {Build Price}: a project gallery, a design-visit form, a permits page and a few town pages. Less than the railing on one deck."

email.subject: Deck site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for deck builders in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll text you the link. Have a look when you're off the frame. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} deck demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Should I leave it up for you? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, people are starting to plan spring decks and pergolas, and the design-visit requests are about to pick up. Thought of you.

The sample site is still here if you want another look, same price as before: {demo-link}

bullets: Price the gallery by project type: decks, pergolas and covered patios each get their own section and their own price line.
A design-visit form that asks deck size, height off the ground and board preference is worth more than a contact form. Charge for it separately.
Peg the build to the railing on one mid-size deck, never to an hourly rate.
Quote a permits and inspection page only for builders who pull their own permits; otherwise leave it out.
Charge more when the builder sells design-and-build with drawings, because the site has to show plans as well as finished decks.
Keep the repair and resurfacing page cheap and quick; it is the door most deck rebuilds walk through.

lineItems.description: Max with before-and-after pairs, a short write-up per deck and filters for board type and railing.

lineItems.item: Design-visit form with deck size and height
lineItems.description: Max with yard picture upload, a sketch field, HOA status and routing to the right designer.
Max when it covers several towns' permit steps and a printable checklist for the homeowner.

lineItems.item: Pergola and patio cover comparison page
lineItems.description: Max with a side-by-side of open, louvered and solid covers and a gallery for each.
Max when each town page gets its own finished decks and local permit notes.

lineItems.item: Deck repair and resurfacing landing page
lineItems.description: Max with a symptom checker for soft boards and wobbly rails and a fast inspection request.
Max when it includes a narrated walk around three finished decks with captions.

whatElseYouSell.name: Golden-hour deck photo and drone shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One evening at your three best decks, ground and drone, with the pergola lights on. That's the gallery and a season of posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or the week they finish a multi-level deck they're proud of.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep with weekly deck posts
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every week a finished deck or pergola goes on your Google profile with the town in the caption, so the listing never looks idle."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live and a new deck is finished.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks timed to the final deck inspection
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When the deck passes final inspection, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review while they're still standing on it."

whatElseYouSell.name: Jobsite sign and truck panel artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A deck under construction gets weeks of attention from the street. A jobsite sign with your name and the site turns that into calls."
whatElseYouSell.when: Right after launch, before the next deck starts framing.

whatElseYouSell.name: Winter design-visit campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A January push for spring decks and pergolas fills your design calendar before the other builders' phones start ringing."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in November, run in January and February.

whatElseYouSell.name: Neighbour door hangers around each deck build
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When a deck goes up, the six houses that can see it get a door hanger with the finished deck on it."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once there are finished decks on the site.

whatElseYouSell.name: Deck and pergola style book for realtors and designers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A printed and online style book of your decks and patio covers puts you in the hands of the agents and designers who get asked 'who built this?'"
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the gallery has enough projects.

whatElseYouSell.name: Spanish-language deck pages
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your deck and patio cover pages in Spanish reach families who'd rather read the details in their own language before the design visit."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if their crew or customers speak Spanish.

withoutAI.route: Paver and patio crews who pour or lay below the deck
withoutAI.whoPays: The hardscaper, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who lays the paver patio at the bottom of your deck stairs? I'll build their site too, and the two link to each other."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Backyard jobs run in sequence and the trades already trade names. One introduction from the deck builder is a warm door.

withoutAI.route: The lumber and composite decking yard
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your lumber yard sells decking to every builder in the county and its site is a phone number. Introduce me and I'll build their builder directory."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Yards have marketing money and their contractor list is the prospect list you'd otherwise build by hand.

withoutAI.route: Electricians who wire deck lighting and outlets
withoutAI.whoPays: The electrician, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The electrician who puts the lights in your pergola beams needs a site as much as you do. Mention me and I'll build it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Sparkies on deck jobs rarely market themselves, and a referral from the deck builder is enough to start.

withoutAI.route: Home inspectors who flag failing decks
withoutAI.whoPays: The inspector, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Home inspectors write up loose ledgers and rotted joists every week. They need a site, and their buyers need a deck builder's number."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: A two-way referral: the inspector sends repair and rebuild jobs, the deck builder recommends the inspector to buyers.

withoutAI.route: HOA management firms that approve deck plans
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The HOA reviews deck and pergola plans by email. I can build them an architectural request page with the setback and height rules on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Deck builders deal with HOA managers constantly. The manager has a real problem and a line item for resident tools.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Everyone who gets a new deck goes shopping for patio furniture the next week. The local shop needs a site that shows furniture on finished decks."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same customer, same month. The deck builder's projects make the shop's site look real.

withAI.route: Deck material estimator for the lumber yard's contractors
withAI.pitchLine: "Give every deck builder on your accounts a tool that turns a deck sketch into a joist, beam and board list priced from your yard."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties builders to one yard's price sheet, which is worth more to the yard than a rebate.

withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant reads each deck or pergola submission against the HOA's height, setback and colour rules before the board sees it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards meet rarely and a rejected plan wastes a month. The manager pays to stop the resubmissions.

withAI.route: Quote follow-up for the paver crew
withAI.pitchLine: "Patio quotes go cold while the paver crew is on a compactor all day. A text that chases each quote, set up for them the way it runs for your decks."
withAI.whyItWorks: You built it once already. The second build is configuration, and the referral came from a client who trusts you.

withAI.pitchLine: "It turns an inspector's deck findings into a plain repair summary the buyer can forward to a deck builder."
withAI.whyItWorks: Inspectors want buyers to understand their reports, and the deck builder becomes the obvious next call.

withAI.route: Furniture-on-deck visualiser for the patio shop
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers upload a picture of their new deck and see a dining set or sectional placed on it before they buy."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells larger sets, and the deck builder's finished decks are the obvious demo material.

withAI.pitchLine: "Tenants report soft boards and loose rails. An assistant sorts the reports by risk from the description and sends the urgent decks to one builder."
withAI.whyItWorks: A failing rental deck is a liability the manager fears. The deck client gets steady repair work out of it.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for deck enquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When you're up on a frame and miss a call, the caller gets a text asking for the address and whether it's a new deck, a rebuild or a pergola."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their business number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Deck budget calculator by size, height and boards
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner enters the deck size, how high it sits and wood or composite, and sees a realistic range before the design visit. Fewer drives to people expecting a patio-set price."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real price per square foot by board type, railing upcharges and their minimum job.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and draw invoicing for deck builds
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit at signing, a draw when the frame passes inspection, the balance when the last railing is on, each sent with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit and draw rules and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts that name the deck project
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new review gets a reply drafted in your voice that mentions the deck or pergola by name, ready to approve on your phone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the review asks. Needs ten past replies to learn the voice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deck project board from design visit to final inspection
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every deck from the design visit through permit, footings, framing inspection and final on one board, instead of a whiteboard in the shop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once the form is bringing in requests. Needs their stages, who designs, and how permits are tracked.

softwareAI.name: Permit packet builder for deck plans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the deck size, height and footing layout, and it prints the permit packet: site plan, framing plan and the ledger detail the town wants."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, or the first time a permit bounces. Needs two past approved deck permits and their standard framing details.

softwareAI.name: After-hours deck intake assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers late calls, asks new deck or repair, rough size and timeline, and books the design visit. You hear the recording in the morning."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once they trust you. Needs their calendar, service list and the questions they always ask. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Photo-to-concept deck sketcher
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads a picture of the back of the house and gets two rough deck and pergola layouts to react to before you visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a set of past before-and-after decks to tune against and their standard layouts. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Framing takeoff from the deck plan
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Draw the deck outline and height and it lists footings, posts, beams, joists, hangers and boards for the lumber order, for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their span rules, joist spacing and a few past material lists. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Homeowner portal with plan approval and build dates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner signs off the deck plan and railing choice, sees permit status and the build date, and stops texting to ask."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the project board in place first.

softwareAI.name: Inspection-day reminder flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When footings are dug, the footing inspection request and the homeowner notice go out on the right day, so the crew isn't standing around."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their towns' inspection steps and who calls the inspector.

softwareAI.name: Deck and pergola chatbot on boards, permits and lead times
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do I need a permit for a low deck' and 'how soon can you start' at midnight, using only your rules and your schedule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their board options, permit notes and current lead time, refreshed monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by deck type and crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether composite decks, pergolas or covered patios actually make you the most once lumber, hardware and crew days are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of lumber invoices and crew days per deck.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-estimate notes for the deck walk
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the yard, talk through the deck size, stairs and railing, and it drafts the estimate with demo of the old deck included."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their estimate template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with footing and framing photo checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The crew checks off footing depth, ledger flashing and joist hangers with a photo at each step, so you see every deck without driving to it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, when they run two crews. Needs their build checklist and a lead carpenter willing to test it.

softwareAI.name: Writer for deck project write-ups and town pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Your deck job notes turn into one project story a month, footings to final, and you read it on the couch before it publishes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their job notes and their sign-off on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deck care and anniversary check-in sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A year after the deck goes in, the owner gets a care reminder and an offer to add a pergola or lighting. That's the second project from someone who already said yes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a list of past decks with build dates and their add-on offers.

softwareAI.name: Lumber price-sheet updater
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Composite boards jumped again? Load the new lumber sheet once and every deck range on the site and in your estimates moves with it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the calculator. Needs the yard's price sheet format.

softwareAI.name: Change-order tracker for deck builds
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the homeowner adds a step light or wider stairs mid-build, the change is priced, signed on their phone and added to the final invoice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their change-order pricing and the invoicing flow already set up.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for deck carpenters
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for framer and helper roles answer your usual questions about framing experience, tools and a ride, and you only call the good ones."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post for a carpenter. Needs their must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the deck budget calculator for every builder
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a deck budget calculator for one builder. Every deck outfit in the state loses evenings to the same tyre-kicker visits."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The hard part of vertical software is the workflow. The first deck client taught it and paid for the build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Builder directory licensed to a composite decking distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Put a find-a-deck-builder map on your site for every contractor who buys your boards. They stay loyal to the distributor that sends them decks."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors already spend on dealer loyalty, and a locator their builders depend on outlasts a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certified-installer portal for a pergola kit maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who buy your louvered pergolas ask who can put them up. A portal where certified crews register warranties and show up on a map answers that."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers have a channel problem and a marketing budget. The deck client is the proof that you know the install side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member deck builder a site template, a design-visit form and a permits page as a membership perk."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need reasons to renew, and one agreement reaches dozens of owners who already trust it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label deck site template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency keeps landing deck and patio clients and starting from zero. License my deck template with the gallery filters and permits page built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the relationship; you sell them the part you've already finished.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each deck and patio cover territory needs town pages and a design-visit form routed to its own owner. Built once, rolled out to every territory."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many locations on one template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Deck upgrade pages for new-home builders
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your model homes have a bare slider door to nowhere. Put a deck and pergola package on the options sheet and one local builder delivers it after closing."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders like upgrade revenue and organised trade partners. The deck client becomes the default installer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Deck-safety request portal for property management firms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every property you manage gets the same deck inspection and repair request page, with photos and urgency in one place."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Firms with many rentals buy once and roll it out, and rental decks are a standing liability worry.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Seasonal deck material cost note for builders
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly note on where joist, composite and cedar prices are moving, built from the price sheets builders share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders re-price decks every season. Built only from sheets they contribute, it never claims more than it shows.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your contractor desk takes deck orders by phone and fax. A site where builders send a deck list and pick a delivery day frees the counter."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Yards fight to keep contractor accounts, and the deck builder can tell you exactly what the counter gets wrong.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One deck builder per metro, the next city over
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A new deck builder in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I take one deck builder per metro so the gallery and the calculator stay theirs. {City} is spoken for, the next city isn't."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the finished-deck proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The deck builder left with a half-built site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Somebody started your deck site and vanished before the gallery worked. I can finish it on a deck template that's already live for another builder."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already decided to buy. They need someone who can show finished deck work quickly.

upsellLadder.offer: Deck site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The deck site and the care plan go on one contract, so adding a finished pergola is a text to me, not your Sunday."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks at final inspection and Google profile upkeep
upsellLadder.trigger: The first deck finished since launch passes final inspection.
upsellLadder.line: "That deck just passed final. Let's get the review and the post up while the homeowner is still out on it."

upsellLadder.offer: Golden-hour deck photo and drone shoot
upsellLadder.trigger: They post a multi-level deck or pergola they're proud of, or the gallery still has only a few projects.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot your three best decks one evening with the pergola lights on. The gallery and a season of posts come out of it."

upsellLadder.offer: Deck budget calculator by size, height and boards
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of form data shows the same deck sizes and board choices again and again.
upsellLadder.line: "Most of your deck requests are the same three sizes. A calculator gives them a range before you drive out."

upsellLadder.trigger: The missed-call log shows evening deck calls, or they mention losing a job to a faster callback.
upsellLadder.line: "Those late deck calls are people planning after dinner. This answers them and books the design visit."

upsellLadder.offer: Permit packet builder for deck plans
upsellLadder.trigger: A deck permit gets bounced back by the town, or they mention a week lost to paperwork.
upsellLadder.line: "That bounced deck permit is the reason for this. The packet goes in complete the first time."

upsellLadder.offer: Deck project board from design visit to final inspection
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a second crew or a backlog of several months.
upsellLadder.line: "Two deck crews and a long backlog won't live on a whiteboard. Let's put every deck on one board."

upsellLadder.offer: Deck care and anniversary check-in sequence
upsellLadder.trigger: The first anniversary of the earliest decks built since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "Last spring's decks are a year old. A care reminder with a pergola offer is the easiest second project you'll sell."
